chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥasan ibn Ziyād al-Ṣayqal, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who forgot the first prayer until he had prayed two rakʿahs of al-ʿAṣr. He said: “Then let him make it the first prayer, and let him restart al-ʿAṣr.” I said: If he forgot al-Maghrib until he had prayed two rakʿahs of al-ʿIshāʾ, then remembered? He said: “Then let him complete his prayer, then afterward make up al-Maghrib.” He said: I said to him: May I be made your ransom, you said that when he forgot al-Ẓuhr then remembered while he was in al-ʿAṣr, he should make it the first prayer and then restart; yet for this one you said he completes his prayer, then afterward makes up al-Maghrib. So he said: “This is not like that. Indeed, after al-ʿAṣr there is no prayer, whereas after al-ʿIshāʾ there is a prayer.”

key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first prayer, here referring contextually to the earlier obligatory prayer
key_terms.فَلْيَجْعَلْهَا: let him count it as, meaning to reassign the intention of the prayer
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ: let him complete the prayer he is in
key_terms.لْيَقْضِ: let him make up the missed prayer afterward
key_terms.وَلْيَسْتَأْنِفِ: let him begin again or restart

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they remember a missed earlier prayer while praying a later one?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on one who forgets an earlier obligatory salat and remembers during a later one. It distinguishes between forgetting al-Ẓuhr and remembering during al-ʿAṣr, versus forgetting al-Maghrib and remembering during al-ʿIshāʾ, based on the order of prayers and what remains after the current prayer.
